- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and model shows upward trend, check for overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak if spike occurred.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–3 day lag in price drop.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce slope by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and model is trending upward, consider downward bias; add 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, reset forecast to align with recent 7-day mean, then apply sentiment-adjusted trend.
